component.name: ComputeSec
component.summary: Evaluate firmware, kernel hardening, hardware vendor and usage habits
评估固件安全、内核加固、硬件品牌与使用习惯

description.p: ComputeSec is a friendly GTK4/libadwaita assistant that helps you turn a Linux machine into a trustworthy computing environment.

ul.li: Dashboard with an overall security score
fwupd Host Security ID (HSI) results with plain-language explanations and a “You can fix” section
Kernel command line and sysctl hardening comparison with copy-and-paste fixes
Hardware vendor reputation database (Superfish, ShadowHammer, Boot Guard key leaks, etc.)
Usage habits: Flatpak adoption, uptime, 2.4G wireless receivers, NTFS/Windows presence

description.p: All checks run locally and never upload data. Results that need root privileges are collected via a step-by-step wizard that reads from the clipboard, without requesting invasive permissions like flatpak-spawn.
ComputeSec 是一个基于 GTK4/libadwaita 的桌面小工具，帮助您评估固件安全 (HSI)、内核加固程度、硬件品牌信誉与日常使用习惯，并给出可操作的修复建议。所有检测均在本地完成，不会上传任何数据；对于需要 root 权限的信息，我们会通过分步向导引导您自行执行只读命令并复制结果。

screenshot.caption: Dashboard with overall score and security sections
仪表盘展示综合评分与四大安全板块

description.p: Correctness fixes for readings taken from a snapshot or over the network.

ul.li: Outside Flatpak, live /proc values now win over a snapshot taken earlier in the same boot; the snapshot only fills in entries that cannot be read (such as vm.mmap_rnd_bits). Previously a revoked sysctl could still be reported as hardened
A snapshot entry that fills an unreadable key is labelled with its age, so an hours-old value no longer looks live

The version check has an overall deadline, not just a per-socket timeout, so a slow trickle can no longer leave the retry button silent; repeated clicks are queued instead of dropped, and a late result from an earlier check is discarded
"Could not verify the kernel version line" no longer blames the network when the local kernel release string itself cannot be parsed, and never prints empty parentheses
Usage Habits: entries that could not be read no longer deduct points, matching the other three sections
2.4G receiver detection ignores guitars, MIDI gear, remote controls, barcode scanners and printers that happen to be named "USB Receiver"
The collection wizard shows the real data directory instead of a hard-coded ~/.local/share/computesec
Unknown options and conflicting options are rejected instead of being ignored
Dropped the Flathub manifest (Flathub submission is no longer planned); the metainfo release version is now checked against the application version in CI

description.p: Detection accuracy, network hardening and packaging fixes.

ul.li: Bluetooth adapters, IR receivers, TV tuners and similar devices are no longer reported as confirmed 2.4G receivers; receivers that only say "Receiver" or "Dongle" are reported as suspected without deducting points
A bare slab_debug, and comma-separated intel_iommu / amd_iommu / iommu options, are now judged the way the kernel parses them
"Check kernel version line again" really contacts kernel.org instead of re-reading the 24-hour cache, and reports the result
The version check rejects every redirect hop that is not HTTPS, not just the final address
A corrupted host data cache can no longer break the Kernel page
The pip-installed computesec command shares run.py's options (--version, --help, --install) and works without a graphical session
Root-only sysctls missing from a snapshot taken without sudo are shown as unreadable again, with the matching hint
The Flathub manifest gains the network permission already present in the JSON manifest
Python 3.12 or newer is now required, matching every distribution that ships libadwaita 1.4

The Kernel page now says so when the kernel.org version check could not run, with a retry button, instead of silently showing nothing; a conclusion taken from an expired cache is labelled with its age
Scores are rounded instead of truncated, so the overall score is no longer systematically one point too low
The version check limits response size and rejects redirects that downgrade to plain HTTP
Repeated version checks no longer spawn duplicate background threads
run.py gains --version and --help, and no longer starts the GUI for unknown options
The package can be installed with pip, which also installs the desktop file, metainfo and icon
CI: fixed path filters (pyproject.toml, conftest.py, scripts, web), least-privilege token, per-job timeouts, pull request runs and a Python 3.9 / 3.13 matrix
Checks the running kernel against the current mainline / stable version lines and warns when LTS branches are used, because they do not carry all upstream security fixes
Network sysctls are no longer read from a Flatpak private network namespace; unverifiable entries are excluded from scoring
Unavailable sections now show "not assessable" instead of a misleading 0, and HSI items fwupd cannot determine are no longer counted as failures
2.4G wireless receivers that cannot be confirmed are reported as "suspected" without deducting points
Host data cache is validated before use and stored with 0600 permissions
Removed the invasive flatpak-spawn (org.freedesktop.Flatpak) permission
New step-by-step data collection wizard that reads results from the clipboard
Root-only sysctl values such as vm.mmap_rnd_bits are now reported instead of silently misjudged
Host OS name and kernel are read over the org.freedesktop.hostname1 D-Bus interface instead of the runtime's /etc/os-release
